proposals.title: Show the number of Dowser proposals on the Confluence page byline
proposals.rationale: The Confluence byline already counts the proposals that name a page, but the count only appears after a reader opens the popup. The team listed showing it in the byline title as an open follow-up. No ticket or goal asks for it, so it is a small doc-promised polish item rather than measured demand.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Put the proposal count in the Dowser byline title on Confluence pages ("Dowser (3)"), so readers see a page is affected without opening the popup.

## Description
The byline resolver already returns a count for each page (`forge/src/core/cards.mjs:269`), and the popup renders it (`forge/static/app/src/routes/byline/index.jsx:64`). The byline module title is a fixed string (`forge/manifest.yml:181`, `forge/manifest.yml:185`), so a page with three affected proposals looks the same as one with none until it is opened. The project status lists this as an open follow-up (`docs/concepts/project-status-and-next-steps.md:202`). Demand: 7 ticket queries since 2026-08-06 (90 days), including the two demand sweeps and `byline OR confluence OR doc impact OR page count`, returned 0 tickets; `dowser_sources_goals` returned 0 goals. Grouping key: none (no tickets). Done means the byline title carries the count when it is above zero and stays "Dowser" otherwise.

## Flow
- add a `dynamicProperties` function to the `dowser-doc-impact` byline item in the manifest
- implement it in the Forge entry point by calling the existing bylineForPage count, limited to visible inboxes
- return the title with the count, plain "Dowser" at zero
- test: a page named by 2 open proposals yields a title with 2; an unnamed page yields "Dowser"

## Expected impact
Confluence readers see at a glance which pages have pending doc changes, which supports the doc-impact demo story. The dynamic-properties call runs on every page view, which adds Forge invocations and SQL reads; it must stay a single cheap count.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Confluence readers see the proposal count without opening the byline
Before: 0 of 1 byline items show a count in the title; the count appears only in the popup
After: the byline title shows the count; checked by opening a page named by a proposal on the live site
Method: quote - read the manifest entry, the resolver return and the popup header; 7 ticket queries counted 0 demand
Falsified if: Forge contentBylineItem dynamicProperties cannot read Forge SQL within its time limit

evidence.quote: - Byline count in the byline title via `dynamicProperties` (today the count shows only in the popup).

proposals.confidence_why: The code and the status doc agree the count exists and is hidden, but 7 ticket queries and the goals source returned nothing; one reader or demand ticket asking for it would raise it.
proposals.impact_why: None: 0 tickets in 90 days across 7 queries and 0 goals; a doc-promised capability-exists claim only.
proposals.predicted_why: No similar decision in near or outcomes. The team listed it as its own follow-up, but with no demand and the Dec 1 gate ahead it is polish a person will likely park.

proposals.title: Keep the working skill when a reinstall or upgrade fails to write
proposals.rationale: Upgrading deletes the installed skill before copying the new one, so a write error leaves the person with no working Dowser and a bare "write failed" line. A leftover folder can then be refused as "not a Dowser install". Install and upgrade are how every person starts.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Copy the new skill beside the old one and swap it in only once the copy is complete; on failure, say that the old install is untouched and what to try.

## Description
With a target present the installer removes it first (`skill/install.mjs:326`) and only then creates the folder and copies (`skill/install.mjs:330`). Any error in that block ends with `write failed: <node message>` and exit 3 (`skill/install.mjs:335`), with no next step and the previous install already gone. If the removal or copy stops before `SKILL.md` is in place, the next run checks for that file (`skill/install.mjs:251`) and refuses the folder Dowser left behind (`skill/install.mjs:318`), asking the person to move it away by hand. Done means a failed write leaves the old install working, and the message names the folder and the command to run again.

## Flow
- person runs install.mjs over an existing install to upgrade
- the installer deletes the old skill folder
- the copy fails (disk full, permission, antivirus lock)
- the person sees write failed with a Node error and has no working skill
- a rerun may be refused because the leftover folder lacks SKILL.md

## Expected impact
This blocks a person upgrading: the skill that worked a minute ago is gone, and the message does not say how to get it back. After the fix a failed upgrade changes nothing and the message says so. Measure installer exits with code 3 after a successful earlier install. A rename-based swap must stay safe for the --dev-link junction on Windows.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed upgrade never leaves the person without a working skill
Before: delete happens before copy (1 of 1 replace paths); 1 failure message with no next step
After: the old install is removed only after a complete copy; the failure message names the target and the rerun command
Method: quote - read the replace block and the refusal check in install.mjs; no write failure was reproduced (that would mean writing outside the work folder)
Falsified if: fs.cpSync is in fact atomic for a directory tree on the supported platforms, or the harness keeps its own copy of the skill

evidence.quote: fail(`write failed: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`, 3);
fail(`${target} exists and is not a Dowser install; move it away first`, 3);

proposals.confidence_why: The order of delete and copy is quoted directly; a reproduced failed upgrade or a support report would raise it.

artifacts.message: The old install is deleted before the copy that can fail
artifacts.alt: Flow of four upgrade steps: run the installer over an existing install, the old install is deleted, the copy fails, write failed is shown with no next step. The copy failure is marked as the failure and the next step as missing.

proposals.impact_why: Blocked, off the main task: a failed upgrade deletes the working skill and gives no next step; reach unmeasured (0 tickets).
proposals.predicted_why: No similar decision in near or outcomes. Staging the copy and swapping it in is a small, local change to the one entry command, and keeping a working install is hard to argue against.

proposals.title: Let a bulk reject or snooze survive one proposal someone else already decided
proposals.rationale: When one checked proposal was decided elsewhere (a teammate, Rovo) during triage, the whole batch is refused, every card comes back as open, and the reason and note typed for it are gone. The message says to reload, but the inbox has no reload control. Triage is the main task of the Jira app, so this hits the person deciding the backlog.
proposals.body:
## Summary
When a reject or snooze meets a proposal that is no longer open, decide the rest, show the conflicting one in its real status, and keep the reason and note.

## Description
The bulk path checks every ref before deciding any (`forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:194`), and one decided card throws a bare "is accepted, not open" (`forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:138`); the single-card race says "reload it" (`forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:123`). The inbox then restores every ref of the batch as open (`forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/useVerdicts.js:65`) and shows the server text followed by "It is back in the list." (`forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/useVerdicts.js:67`), so the toast reads "Could not reject 5 proposals: DW-7 is accepted, not open It is back in the list." The restored cards show the error above live Accept and Reject buttons (`forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/ReadingPane.jsx:29`). `git grep -i reload` over `routes/inbox` finds one reload control, in the load-error state only (`forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/index.jsx:146`); the toolbar has none. The reason and note live only in the closed Reject dialog, so a retry means choosing and typing them again. Ticket query `error OR stuck OR confusing OR "can't" OR lost OR accessibility OR "screen reader"` since 2026-05-08 returned 0 tickets, so reach is unmeasured. Done means the other cards are decided, the conflicting one shows its current status, and nothing typed has to be typed again.

## Flow
- person checks 5 proposals, presses r, picks a reason and types a note
- meanwhile DW-7 is accepted by a teammate or through Rovo
- after the 6-second undo window verdict.reject refuses the whole batch
- all 5 come back as open, with an error toast that runs two sentences together
- person finds no reload control, refreshes the Jira page, re-checks 4 cards and retypes the reason and note

## Expected impact
This blocks the triager on the error branch of the main inbox task: the batch is lost along with the note they wrote. After the fix they read one toast and carry on. Measure the share of failed reject and snooze calls that end in a second call for the same refs. Deciding part of a batch changes the all-or-nothing contract that the Rovo and MCP callers of the resolver may rely on.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one conflicting card no longer costs the whole batch or the typed note
Before: 7 steps to finish a 5-card reject after one conflict; 0 reload controls outside the load-error state; the batch of 5 is refused for 1 conflict
After: 1 step (read the toast: 4 rejected, DW-7 already accepted); the reason and note are kept
Method: count - read the reject path from the resolver to the toast and counted the reload controls in routes/inbox with git grep
Falsified if: verdict.reject is in fact called with only the still-open refs, or the inbox reloads on its own after a failed decision

evidence.quote: Resolves `refs` and checks every one is open before deciding any (a bulk decision is all-or-nothing up front).
throw new AppError('bad-input', `${p.ref} is ${p.status}, not open`);
throw new AppError('bad-input', `${p.ref} is ${now.status}, not open; reload it`);
${message} It is back in the list.`, 'error');

proposals.confidence_why: The resolver and the UI restore path are quoted directly; a reproduced two-tab race or a ticket from a triager would raise it.

artifacts.message: One card decided elsewhere refuses the whole batch and offers no reload
artifacts.alt: Flow of five triage steps: check 5 proposals, pick a reason and type a note, a teammate accepts one, the batch is refused and all 5 return as open, no reload control. The refusal is marked as the failure and the reload as missing.

artifacts.message: Finishing the batch after one conflict drops from 7 steps to 1
artifacts.alt: Before and after of the steps to finish a 5-card reject after one card was decided elsewhere. Before: dismiss toast, refresh the Jira page, re-check 4 cards, press r, pick reason, retype note, confirm. After: read one toast.

proposals.impact_why: Blocked on the error branch of the main triage task: one conflict refuses the batch and drops the typed note; 0 tickets in 180 days, reach unmeasured.
proposals.predicted_why: No similar decision in near or outcomes. The inbox already invests in undo windows and error restore, so a gap that loses a batch and a typed note on the main screen fits work the team keeps.

proposals.title: Name the field and the line when lens direction cannot be saved
proposals.rationale: A team lead who types eleven topics into "Leave out" is told "exclude holds 11 items; at most 10", a field name the screen never shows. An over-long line is refused without saying which one. They must work out the fix by trial.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Word the lens direction save errors with the labels on the Settings screen, and name the line that is too long.

## Description
The Settings fields are labelled "Focus on" and "Leave out" (`forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:151`). The resolver validates them under their payload keys (`forge/src/core/direction.mjs:51`) and words its errors with those keys: "exclude holds 11 items; at most 10" (`forge/src/core/direction.mjs:36`) and "each exclude item is one line of at most 120 characters" (`forge/src/core/direction.mjs:38`), which does not say which line. The editor shows the server text as is (`forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:174`). Done means the message uses the screen label and quotes the start of the offending line.

## Flow
- person types 11 topics into Leave out and presses Save
- direction.set refuses: exclude holds 11 items; at most 10
- person maps exclude to Leave out and deletes lines until Save passes

## Expected impact
Slows the person steering a lens: today they decode a field name and hunt for the long line. After the fix the message names the field they see and the line to shorten. The resolver text is also read by MCP callers, so the wording change must keep the bad-input code.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused direction names the field and line the person sees
Before: 2 of 2 list-limit messages name the payload key, not the label; 0 name the offending line
After: 2 of 2 name the label; the long-line message quotes the line
Method: count - read the 2 list-limit throws in direction.mjs and the 2 list labels in the Settings editor
Falsified if: the Settings editor rewrites resolver messages before showing them

evidence.quote: throw new AppError('bad-input', `${key} holds ${out.length} items; at most ${DIRECTION_ITEMS_MAX}`);
throw new AppError('bad-input', `each ${key} item is one line of at most ${DIRECTION_LINE_MAX} characters`);

proposals.confidence_why: Label, validator and display are quoted from two files; a ticket from someone who hit the limit would raise it.
proposals.impact_why: Slowed, off the core path: Settings errors name the payload key exclude instead of the Leave out label, and not the line.
proposals.predicted_why: No similar decision in near or outcomes. The hint under the fields already states the limits, so a copy fix on a rarely hit Settings error is likely judged not worth a ticket.

proposals.title: Make the Jira app install steps build the inbox UI on a fresh clone
proposals.rationale: The guide the README links for connecting Jira tells you to install the app's packages and then build its inbox screen, but the install step never fetches the screen's build tool. On a fresh clone the second command fails, so a first-time admin cannot get the inbox onto their site by following the steps.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Add the Custom UI install (`npm --prefix static/app install`) to the "Install on a development site" steps before `npm run build:ui`, so the documented sequence works on a fresh clone.

## Description
The guide runs `npm install` in `forge/` (`docs/forge-app.md:145`) and then `npm run build:ui` (`docs/forge-app.md:146`). That script is `npm --prefix static/app run build` (`forge/package.json:15`), which runs `vite build` (`forge/static/app/package.json:10`); `vite` is a devDependency of `forge/static/app` only (`forge/static/app/package.json:20`), and `static/app` has its own lockfile. `npm install` in `forge/` installs `forge/package.json` alone. Checks: no `workspaces` in `forge/package.json` or the root `package.json`, no `postinstall` or `prebuild:ui` hook in either, and the section is not scoped to an already-set-up checkout. The README sends first-time users to this section (`README.md:69`). The local-run section has the same gap: `npm run local:ui` (`docs/forge-app.md:396`) also needs `static/app` installed, which only the separate "Running the UI outside Jira" section does. Not executed (the pack forbids installing to check). Done means the install block on a fresh clone builds `static/app/dist` with no extra step.

## Flow
- admin clones the repo and follows "Install on a development site"
- `npm install` in forge/ installs the backend packages only
- `npm run build:ui` fails: vite is not found in static/app

## Expected impact
First-time admins and Codegeist judges get the Jira inbox deployed by following the guide as written. Measured by running the block on a fresh clone. Low risk: a one-line doc change.

## Evaluation
Claim: docs - the documented install block builds the Custom UI on a fresh clone
Before: 1 build command whose tool (vite) no listed step installs; 0 install steps for forge/static/app in the section
After: 1 install step for forge/static/app before the build; the block runs clean on a fresh clone
Method: quote - read the two doc lines and the three package.json lines; not run, since checking would mean installing
Falsified if: `npm install` in forge/ is shown to install forge/static/app dependencies (a workspace or hook not found here)

evidence.quote: npm run build:ui                 # builds static/app/dist, the Custom UI resource
([docs/forge-app.md](docs/forge-app.md#install-on-a-development-site)), then add its MCP server to
npm run local:ui        # terminal 2: the Custom UI (vite --mode local) at http://127.0.0.1:5173, POSTing to :4710

proposals.confidence_why: Sure, tier 1: doc and package.json lines quoted and no workspace or install hook found; running the block on a fresh clone would make it certain.

artifacts.message: The install block builds the UI with vite, which no step of the block installs
artifacts.alt: Table of the install steps and package scripts: forge-app.md runs npm install in forge then npm run build:ui; forge/package.json maps build:ui to static/app; static/app runs vite build and lists vite as its own devDependency.

proposals.impact_why: Tier 1, a documented step fails: the README-linked Jira install stops at npm run build:ui on a fresh clone.
proposals.predicted_why: No similar decision in near or outcomes. A sure first-run break in the setup guide with both sides quoted, fixed by one doc line; nothing suggests the team would turn it down.

proposals.title: Status page sends new sessions after two items that already shipped
proposals.rationale: The project status page, which every new session is told to read first, lists two pieces of work as still to do that the code already has. A session following its next steps would redo finished work before reaching what is actually open.
proposals.body:
## Summary
Mark live-test gap 3 (the "NEW" badge on decided cards) and the per-proposal `delivery_risk` item as done in the status page, so its open list and next steps name only open work.

## Description
Gap 3: the page says gap 3 is still open (`docs/concepts/project-status-and-next-steps.md:138`, described at `:162`) and makes fixing it next step 1 (`:175`). The card component shows the change marker only for open items (`forge/static/app/src/components/ProposalCard.jsx:140`, with the comment at `:138`), added in commit 85fb5c0 (2026-10-28), a day before the page marked the other gaps fixed. Per-proposal delivery risk: next step 7 still plans "a lens (or a skill step) that fills `delivery_risk`" (`:191`), while `verify` now measures each card's bus factor from git and writes it into `delivery_risk.bus_factor` (`skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:16`, `:19`), since commit 7b6f408 (2026-10-30); the page's own table already says every lens fills `delivery_risk`. Checks: the page is a living status doc, not historical; no feature flag keeps the old badge; no other open item covers either. Gap 5 (not exercised live) stays open and is not part of this card. Done means the open list and next steps hold no shipped work.

## Flow
- a new session opens the status page first, as AGENTS.md says
- it takes next step 1 (gap 3) or step 7 (delivery_risk) as open
- it re-investigates work that already shipped

## Expected impact
Sessions start on real open work (gap 5, the first real-repository run, the Rovo live test). Measured by the count of shipped items in the open list. Low risk: one doc.

## Evaluation
Claim: docs - the status page's open items match the code
Before: 2 items listed as open whose code is shipped (gap 3, per-proposal delivery_risk)
After: 0 shipped items in "Still open" and "Next steps"
Method: quote - read the doc lines, the component and verify.mjs, plus the commits that added them
Falsified if: the NEW badge still shows on decided cards in the live inbox (a path other than ProposalCard renders it)
